title: Servant Leadership
definition: Servant Leadership is Christlike leadership that uses authority to serve, protect, equip, and build up others rather than to dominate them.
summary: Servant Leadership is Christlike leadership that uses authority to serve, protect, equip, and build up others rather than to dominate them.
christFocus: Jesus came not to be served but to serve, giving His life as the model and power for humble leadership among His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Servant leadership is shaped by the cross. It does not reject responsibility or authority, but it refuses to use authority for selfish ambition, control, or status.

Jesus redefined greatness by washing feet and giving His life. In the Church, leadership should look like humble service, patient care, truthful instruction, and sacrificial love.

Servant leadership depends on the Holy Spirit because pride comes naturally to fallen hearts. Christ forms leaders who are willing to decrease so others may grow in Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People who have experienced controlling leadership may struggle to believe authority can be safe. Servant leadership shows the heart of Christ, who uses power to rescue and restore rather than exploit.

This doctrine also challenges every leader, whether pastor, teacher, parent, recovery sponsor, or ministry servant, to measure influence by faithfulness rather than attention.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use whatever influence you have to serve others in Christ’s name. Lead with humility, listen carefully, protect the vulnerable, tell the truth in love, and depend on the Spirit to make your leadership reflect Jesus.
